sections: Abstract

We report retention rate measurements from five monitoring stations collected between 2023 and 2025. A pilot survey in 2020 had put the regional retention rate at 27.5 %; we find marked differences between upland and coastal sites.
1. Introduction
Earlier studies of phoneme drift relied on single-site records [1, 2]. A multi-site campaign makes it possible to separate local effects from regional trends [3].
2. Methods

Station metadata are listed in Table 1. Measurements follow the protocol of [3]. Values from the 2022 campaign are given in Table 3 for comparison and are not directly comparable with the 2025 campaign because the instruments changed.
3. Results
Table 2 reports the retention rate for each station in the 2025 campaign. The largest change relative to 2022 was observed at station B-04.
4. Discussion
The spread between stations exceeds the measurement uncertainty, which suggests that site conditions dominate. Longer records are needed to confirm the trend.
References
[1] Abernathy et al. (2019). [2] Jovanović and Rasmussen (2021). [3] Petrenko et al. (2022).
